terms.comment: Counsel, and then the body that gives it: a general’s council, the elders of Carthage (see council, an advisory body). Morgan–Owens gives it for a committee, and cōnsilium ex utrāque factiōne collēctum for a panel drawn from both parties (s.v. bipartisan). A Roman board was named by its number: trēsvirī, decemvirī.

terms.gloss: an assembly; Traupman’s word for a committee
terms.comment: Classically an assembly called to take counsel (see council, an advisory body).

phrases.english: a committee drawn from both parties

sources: Lewis & Short: consilium · Lewis & Short: concilium
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. committee, commission; bipartisan.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 178, 294.
